objectives: Identify the shared sm onset in taught words.
Compare word endings while reading every grapheme accurately.
Group words by a shared ending without confusing onset and rime.
Read controlled word chains and explain the feature that stays the same or changes.
concepts: The onset is the beginning consonant sound or blend before the vowel.
The rime contains the vowel and following sounds.
Words can share an onset while having different rimes.
Word-family work still requires decoding each complete word.

definitions.definition: The initial consonant sound or blend before the vowel.
The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
A group of words that share a spelling or sound pattern.

workedExamples.solution: Both begin with sm; their endings differ.
Both begin with sm, but the rime and word length differ.

workedExamples.prompt: How do you sort a new sm-word?

commonMistakes: Sorting by first letter only and ignoring the m.

keyTakeaways: Read the rest of each word carefully.
